title: Design System: A Thread Through Night

scenicUtilityGrounds.scope: Opaque text-sized onward link and caption grounds only; reading chapters unboxed and mint label copy/grounds preserved; mobile utility spacing corrected.

portraitMoon.status: Blocked private raster is NOT publishable. Current served old PNGs are tested unchanged; provenance gate remains closed.

shadows.name: menu-sheet
shadows.purpose: Separate the direct chapter menu from scenery.

extensions.lightControls: local filament/exposure feedback; native camera range; old-poster brightness reduced-motion alternative
extensions.ambientBudget: visible-only water, 24fps maximum, pause/offscreen/hidden stop draws

motion.name: scene-ready
motion.purpose: Reveal a successfully rendered scene; removed under reduced motion.

components.name: Onward text link
components.description: A plainly underlined native onward anchor.

components.name: LinkedIn contact
components.description: The only real outbound contact route.

narrative.overview: An authored open-water landscape gives way to plain, spacious reading. The surface alternates physical depth and typographic quiet, instead of asking visitors to read substantial text on scenery. Original terrain is illustrative, not a claim about real places or projects.
keyCharacteristics: Three continuous terrain/water compositions with palette shifts.
Lightweight, open sans display and ordinary readable body copy.
Native anchors and a disclosure menu; no content gates or scroll hijack.

rules.name: The Chapter Field Rule
rules.body: Color occupies whole chapters, not identical accent cards.

rules.name: The Plain Reading Rule
rules.body: Long factual text remains HTML on a quiet color field.

dos: Do preserve whole-field color and uninterrupted readable text.
Do keep visitor movement native and direct access immediate.
Do retain original asset provenance and local font/library licenses.
donts: Don’t introduce fabricated work or copied reference assets.
Don’t turn paragraphs into interchangeable card grids.
Don’t present technical test success as reference-level visual acceptance.
